04-01.t: Birth of Transplant Pioneer Joseph E. Murray
04-01.s: American surgeon Joseph Edward Murray was born; he performed the first successful human kidney transplant and won the 1990 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

04-02.s: American physician Valentine Seaman was born; he introduced the smallpox vaccine to the United States, mapped yellow fever in New York City, and advanced nursing education.

04-03.s: French physician Pierre-Fidèle Bretonneau was born; he identified typhoid fever, named diphtheria, and pioneered the concept that diseases can be caused by bacteria.

04-04.t: Birth of Neurologist John Hughlings Jackson
04-04.s: English neurologist John Hughlings Jackson, renowned for his foundational research on epilepsy and co-founding the journal Brain, was born.
Cardiovascular surgeon Dr. Denton Cooley implanted the first temporary total artificial heart in a human patient.

04-05.t: Incorporation of the American Birth Control League
04-05.s: The American Birth Control League, the forerunner of Planned Parenthood, was officially incorporated on this day.

04-05.t: Death of Hepatitis B Discoverer Baruch Samuel Blumberg
04-05.s: American physician Baruch Samuel Blumberg, who identified the hepatitis B virus, developed its diagnostic test and vaccine, and won the 1976 Nobel Prize, died.

04-06.t: Birth of Neurosurgery Pioneer Walter Dandy
04-06.s: American neurosurgeon Walter Dandy, considered one of the founding fathers of neurosurgery and credited with describing cerebrospinal fluid circulation, was born.
German biochemist Feodor Felix Konrad Lynen was born; he shared the 1964 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering how cholesterol and fatty acid metabolism are regulated.

04-07.t: Founding of the World Health Organization (WHO)
04-07.s: The United Nations established the World Health Organization as a coordinating authority on international public health, commemorated annually as World Health Day.

04-08.t: Birth of Johns Hopkins Founding Dean William Henry Welch
04-08.s: American pathologist and bacteriologist William Henry Welch, first dean of the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine and founder of the first U.S. school of public health, was born.

04-08.t: Birth of Harvey Cushing, Father of Modern Neurosurgery
04-08.s: American neurosurgeon Harvey Williams Cushing, the first exclusive neurosurgeon and first to describe Cushing's disease, was born in Cleveland, Ohio.

04-09.t: Death of American College of Surgeons Co-Founder James Edwin Thompson
04-09.s: English-born surgeon James Edwin Thompson, a founding member and first vice-president of the American College of Surgeons, died on this day.

04-09.t: Death of Public Health Pioneer Milton Joseph Rosenau
04-09.s: Influential American public health official and professor Milton Joseph Rosenau passed away in Chapel Hill, North Carolina.

04-10.s: German physician Samuel Hahnemann, best known for creating the alternative medical system of homeopathy, was born.
Argentine physiologist Bernardo Houssay was born; he shared the 1947 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering how pituitary hormones regulate blood sugar.

04-11.s: English apothecary and surgeon James Parkinson, who authored the 1817 Essay on the Shaking Palsy describing what became known as Parkinson's disease, was born.

04-12.t: Birth of Biochemist Otto Fritz Meyerhof
04-12.s: German physician and biochemist Otto Fritz Meyerhof was born; he shared the 1922 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his work on muscle metabolism.

04-12.t: Salk Polio Vaccine Declared Safe and Effective
04-12.s: Following massive nationwide field trials, Jonas Salk's inactivated polio vaccine was officially declared safe, effective, and potent.

04-13.t: Birth of Physiologist Jean Pierre Flourens
04-13.s: French physiologist Jean Pierre Flourens was born; through animal experiments he first proved that the mind resides in the brain rather than the heart.

04-13.t: Birth of Cholesterol Researcher Michael Stuart Brown
04-13.s: American geneticist Michael Stuart Brown was born; he shared the 1985 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for describing the regulation of cholesterol metabolism.

04-14.t: Completion of the Human Genome Project
04-14.s: The international Human Genome Project was completed, sequencing 99% of the human genome to an accuracy of 99.99%.

04-15.t: Birth of Cardiologist and Biochemist Robert Lefkowitz
04-15.s: American physician-scientist Robert Joseph Lefkowitz was born; he won the 2012 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for revealing the workings of G protein-coupled receptors.

04-16.t: Birth of Pediatric Neurosurgeon James T. Goodrich
04-16.s: American pediatric neurosurgeon James Tait Goodrich, globally recognized for performing multiple successful separations of craniopagus conjoined twins, was born.

04-17.t: Birth of Surgical Pioneer Francis Daniels Moore
04-17.s: American surgeon Francis Daniels Moore was born; he refined burn-treatment techniques, helped perform the first successful organ transplant, and measured body composition using radioisotopes.

04-18.t: Birth of Polio Virologist John R. Paul
04-18.s: American virologist John Rodman Paul, whose research focused on the spread of poliomyelitis and the development of treatments for the disease, was born.

04-19.s: American chemist Glenn T. Seaborg, known for co-discovering iodine-131 used in the diagnosis and treatment of thyroid disease, was born.

04-19.t: Albert Hofmann Conducts First Intentional LSD Experiment
04-19.s: Swiss chemist Albert Hofmann intentionally ingested 0.25 mg of LSD-25 and rode his bicycle home, initiating decades of research into psychedelics and psychiatric neurochemistry.

04-20.t: First Surgical Replacement of a Human Organ
04-20.s: Romanian surgeon Dan Gavriliu performed the first surgical replacement of a human organ (an esophagus) on this day.

04-21.t: Birth of Vitamin Researcher Paul Karrer
04-21.s: Swiss organic chemist Paul Karrer, remembered for his foundational research on vitamins, was born on this day.

04-22.s: Italian neurologist Rita Levi-Montalcini was born in Turin; she won the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering nerve growth factor.
The first human eye transplant procedure was performed on this day in 1969.

04-23.s: Danish pathologist Johannes Fibiger, recipient of the 1926 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, was born in Silkeborg, Denmark.

04-23.t: U.S. Announces Discovery of the Virus Causing AIDS
04-23.s: U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Margaret Heckler held a press conference announcing the discovery of the retrovirus (later named HIV) that causes AIDS.

04-24.t: Sabin Sunday Launches Mass Oral Polio Vaccination in the U.S.
04-24.s: Known as 'Sabin Sunday,' thousands of Greater Cincinnati residents received Albert Sabin's oral polio vaccine on sugar cubes in its first large-scale U.S. deployment.

04-24.t: Death of Influenza Virologist Nancy J. Cox
04-24.s: World-renowned virologist and pandemic preparedness leader Dr. Nancy J. Cox, who led the CDC's Influenza Division from 1992 to 2014, passed away at age 77.

04-25.t: Sigmund Freud Opens His First Private Practice
04-25.s: Dr. Sigmund Freud opened his first private practice as a neurologist in Vienna, marking the clinical starting point of psychoanalysis.

04-25.t: Watson and Crick Publish DNA Double Helix Structure
04-25.s: Francis Crick and James Watson's landmark paper describing the double-helix structure of DNA was published in the journal Nature.

04-26.t: World's First Human Open Fetal Surgery Performed
04-26.s: Dr. Michael Harrison performed the world's first human open fetal surgery, establishing a new surgical frontier for treating congenital conditions before birth.
A nuclear reactor accident at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in Ukraine caused widespread radiation exposure and acute radiation sickness among responders and residents.

04-27.t: Birth of Endorphin Pioneer Hans Kosterlitz
04-27.s: German-born British biologist Hans Kosterlitz, remembered for his pioneering discovery and characterization of endorphins, was born.
American biologist and biophysicist Alexander Rich, whose MIT team grew the first crystal structure of DNA, passed away.

04-28.t: Death of Physiologist Johannes Peter Müller
04-28.s: German physiologist and comparative anatomist Johannes Peter Müller, who advanced understanding of speech, hearing, blood, and lymph, passed away.

04-29.t: Birth of Epidemiologist R. Palmer Beasley
04-29.s: American epidemiologist R. Palmer Beasley was born; his pioneer research established the causal link between hepatitis B virus infection and liver cancer.

04-30.t: Death of Pathologist William Henry Welch
04-30.s: William Henry Welch, known as the 'Dean of American Medicine' and founding dean of the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine, died at Johns Hopkins Hospital.
